note: Scenario analysis assumes Plaskett wins; it is not a call. No transition team, chief of staff or cabinet picks were found, and no polling. Primary figures are unofficial same-day votes. Cabinet entries are limited to the announced running mate.

nominees.name: Stacey E. Plaskett
nominees.role: Democratic nominee; sitting delegate to Congress
team: Milton Potter, running mate; described as Senate President (St. Thomas Source). Sen. Franklin Johnson spoke at her launch as a supporter.

analysis.assumption: Scenario: assumes Stacey Plaskett wins the Nov. 3, 2026 general election. Not a call or forecast.
analysis.summary: Democrat-to-Democrat handoff from Gov. Albert Bryan Jr. The binding constraint is confirmation, not selection: the Legislature approves every Cabinet-level nominee, and the Bryan Cabinet was not complete until Oct. 22, 2019.
analysis.timing: Inauguration expected Jan. 4, 2027 (first Monday in January per the Revised Organic Act as recalled; verify).
priorities: Two nationally accredited hospitals within six years and a local health workforce (VI Consortium).
Rebuild WAPA using the $4.7 billion already secured (VI Consortium).
Education gains, a 311 line and public dashboards (VI Consortium).
Ticket framed as 'federal access and local execution' (Potter, VI Consortium).
firstMoves: Name Finance, Health and budget leaders first.
Stand up WAPA and hospital project teams.
Send the full nominee slate to the Legislature early; the Bryan Cabinet spanned about 28 departments and offices (vi.gov).
Her Delegate seat passes to the next Delegate (Janelle Sarauw won the Democratic primary; general still pending).
risks: Opponents raised Epstein-related attacks during the campaign; she called them a distraction (VI Consortium).
analysis.pollContext: No polling found. Primary: Plaskett/Potter 46.99% of 9,561 same-day votes (unofficial).
